Anya: Quick heads up — after running int8 quant on the new llama-2-13b variant for the summarization suite, BERTScore dropped by ~0.08 on avg. Anyone else seeing this after quant experiments?

Matt: :eyes: yup saw a similar dip on the codegen evals earlier today. Posting a tiny log snippet.
```
BERTScore (fp16)  : 0.8423
BERTScore (int8)  : 0.7598
mean_norm_before  : 3.10
mean_norm_after   : 1.17
```

Jess: That smells like embedding norm drift -> cosine similarity will shrink if we don't normalize. Our bert_score compute expects normalized vectors, right? (check metrics/bert_score.py)

Anya: We thought it did normalize, but the quant pipeline seems to change distribution (saturation/rounding). From the quant log: `embed_mean_before=0.002, embed_std_before=0.98, embed_std_after=0.37` — which matches the norm change above.

Noah: CI link: https://console.redwood.ai/evals/2145 — also the CI job failed with a metric unit test: `tests/eval_runner/test_metrics.py::test_bert_score_norm`

ci-bot: Build #432 failed — tests/eval_runner/test_metrics.py::test_bert_score_norm AssertionError: cosine diff > 0.03 :bug:

Matt: Hypothesis: our quantizer used per-tensor scale for the embedding matrix, causing scale collapse. Two quick mitigations: 1) do explicit L2-normalize inside bert_score before cos sim, 2) fix quantizer to per-channel symmetric scales. We should do (1) as a bandaid so evals are stable.

Jess: Agreed. Adding normalization is low-risk for the metric since BERTScore semantics are cosine-based. Also add a unit test that simulates quant noise. Example patch for metric compute: 
```python
# metrics/bert_score.py (fragment)
def _cosine_sim(a, b):
    a = a / (np.linalg.norm(a, axis=-1, keepdims=True) + 1e-12)
    b = b / (np.linalg.norm(b, axis=-1, keepdims=True) + 1e-12)
    return (a * b).sum(-1)
```

Matt: Also add an integration test to the eval harness that runs with a fake quantizer: `tests/unit/test_bert_norm.py` -> create random embeddings, apply uniform noise/scaling, assert normalized cosine ~ original cosine within tol.

Anya: I'll open a quick PR with the normalization and tests and run CI. If normalization hides the quant bug we'll still follow up on the quantizer fix. :+1:

(15m later) Anya: Quick CI update — with the normalization patch BERTScore delta reduced to ~0.01 vs fp16 on the summarization set. pass@k and exact-match metrics are basically unchanged. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/7891

Matt: Nice. Please also add a dashboard alert: if mean embedding L2 norm changes > 0.2 we should trigger an eval-regression incident. Add a histogram metric to the eval dashboard so we can see norm shifts per model/version. Link: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/eval-regressions

Jess: We should also tag the model onboarding checklist: when bringing quantized variants, run the `quant-smoke` harness that checks embedding norm + bertscore delta before promoting. I'll add the checklist item.

Anya: tagging infra — @Noah can you own the quantizer follow-up (per-channel quant + symmetric scales + test harness)?

Noah: On it. I'll try per-channel symmetric quant and run a grid across zero_point strategies. Will report back with numbers. :thinking_face:

ci-bot: Build #433 — tests passed. :white_check_mark:

Matt: OK closing this thread for now. Follow-ups: PR #7891 merged (temporary fix), infra ticket #4058 for quantizer changes, dashboard alert added. Thanks everyone. :rocket:
